column1: # ZAP baseline overrides for the public Texas Home Outlet storefront.
# A '#' line above each rule says why it is a false positive here.
# IGNORE removes the rule from the baseline warning count. The HTML report
# still lists the alert. High-severity alerts that are not listed here fail
# the job. Do not IGNORE a high-risk rule without a comment that names the
# Informational. Public pages and assets are cacheable on purpose.
# Private staff responses set their own cache headers, and this scan has no staff session.
# Informational beta notes (non-storable, non-cacheable, or cacheable).
# Public responses are supposed to be cacheable. This scan never sees a staff session.
# Low. Public JavaScript contains Unix-epoch integers from build stamps and libraries.
# Those numbers are not credentials or customer data.
# Informational. ZAP is noting that the storefront is a JavaScript application.
# Medium. ZAP looks for a hidden synchronizer token in HTML forms.
# Staff state changes use a cookie and X-CSRF-Token double-submit (auth/csrf.py),
# which this passive check cannot see. This unauthenticated scan has no staff session.
# Public contact and appointment forms do not protect a logged-in session.
